candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: The dimensionless keyhole depth e* is derived from the given physical quantities related to laser melting of liquid metal. Each input quantity is well-defined and standard in dimensional analysis for heat transfer and fluid flow in laser processing. The density (rho), temperature difference (Tl-T0), laser beam radius (r0), thermal diffusivity (alpha), effective laser power (etaP), heat capacity (cp), and laser scan speed (Vs) are fundamental parameters whose SI base dimensions are known and can be combined to form dimensionless groups such as e*.

variables.physical_definition: Material density, mass per unit volume of the metal.
Temperature difference between melting temperature and ambient temperature.
Laser beam radius, characteristic length scale of the laser spot.
Thermal diffusivity, rate of thermal diffusion through the material.
Effective laser power, energy per unit time delivered by the laser.
Heat capacity, amount of heat required to raise the temperature per unit mass.
Laser scan speed, velocity at which the laser moves over the material surface.
